title: The words a gloss cannot teach
intro: These sit in the top 50 of every Spanish frequency list, and every one of them is a piece of grammar wearing the costume of a word. Read this section before the units; come back to it whenever a sentence refuses to parse.

senses.label: joins clauses
senses.text: Links a second clause to the first. English often drops it; Spanish never does.

senses.label: relative pronoun
senses.text: Covers English that, which, who and whom all at once, for people and things alike.

ex.es: La mujer que trabaja aquí es mi hermana.
ex.en: The woman who works here is my sister.

ex.es: El libro que leí era corto.
ex.en: The book I read was short.

senses.label: than
senses.text: After más or menos it forms the comparison.

ex.es: Es más caro que el otro.
ex.en: It's more expensive than the other one.

items.pitfall: With an accent, qué is the question word what. ¿Qué dices? = What are you saying? Que dices = that you say. The accent is the entire difference.

senses.label: possession
senses.text: Spanish has no apostrophe-s. Ownership is built backwards with de.

senses.label: origin, material, topic
senses.text: Where something is from, what it is made of, what it is about.

items.pitfall: de + el always contracts to del. Never write de el. The same happens with a + el = al.

items.gloss: himself · herself · itself · one · each other
items.he: ממלא תפקיד של התפעל / נפעל / סתמי

senses.label: reflexive
senses.text: The action returns to the subject. Closest to the Hebrew hitpa'el.

ex.es: Mi hijo se lava las manos.

senses.label: reciprocal
senses.text: Two or more people doing it to each other.

ex.en: They met each other at school.

senses.label: impersonal / passive
senses.text: No named actor at all. Where English says one, you, or a passive, Spanish says se. Extremely common on signs.

items.pitfall: A fourth se exists purely for sound: le or les becomes se before lo/la/los/las. Se lo di, never le lo di.

senses.label: object pronoun
senses.text: Stands for a masculine thing or person already mentioned, and goes before the verb.

ex.en: The report? I already finished it.

senses.label: makes a noun from an adjective
senses.text: lo + adjective names the quality itself. There is no English one-word equivalent.

ex.en: The important thing is to start.

senses.label: lo que
senses.text: what, in the sense of the thing which.

ex.en: I don't understand what you want.

items.pitfall: lo is not the masculine of la in the article sense. The article is el. lo never precedes a normal noun.

senses.label: cause, motive
senses.text: The reason behind an action. Looks backwards, at what made it happen.

ex.en: I did it because of you / for your sake.

senses.label: movement through, duration
senses.text: Passing along or across, or how long something lasts.

senses.label: agent and rate
senses.text: The doer in a passive, and prices or rates.

ex.en: It was written by a child.

items.pitfall: See para below. If you can substitute in order to, you need para; if you can substitute because of, you need por.

items.gloss: in order to · for (a recipient) · by (a deadline)

senses.label: purpose, goal
senses.text: Looks forwards, at what the action aims at. Followed by an infinitive.

ex.en: I study in order to learn.

senses.label: recipient, destination
senses.text: Who or where something is headed.

senses.label: deadline
senses.text: The point by which something must be done.

items.pitfall: Trabajo para Ana = Ana is my boss. Trabajo por Ana = I'm covering her shift. One preposition, two very different employment situations.

senses.label: direction, time
senses.text: Motion towards something, or a clock time.

ex.es: Vamos a la playa a las ocho.
ex.en: We're going to the beach at eight.

senses.label: the personal a
senses.text: When the direct object is a specific person, Spanish inserts an a that English has no equivalent for. Skipping it is the single most recognisable foreigner mistake.

ex.en: I see the house. (no a — not a person)

items.pitfall: a + el contracts to al. Voy al banco.

senses.label: negates the verb
senses.text: Always immediately before the verb, and before any object pronouns attached to it.

senses.label: double negatives are correct
senses.text: Unlike English, Spanish requires the second negative. Nada, nadie and nunca after the verb still need no in front of it.

senses.label: already
senses.text: The thing has happened, sooner than expected.

senses.label: ya no — not anymore
senses.text: Marks a state that has ended.

senses.label: now, right away
senses.text: In commands and answers it means immediately.

senses.label: comparison
senses.text: más or menos + adjective + que. Spanish has no -er ending.

ex.es: Hoy hay menos gente que ayer.
ex.en: There are fewer people today than yesterday.

senses.label: superlative
senses.text: Add the article: el/la/los/las más.

ex.es: Es la ciudad más grande del país.
ex.en: It's the biggest city in the country.

items.pitfall: Four comparatives are irregular and refuse más: mejor (better), peor (worse), mayor (older/greater), menor (younger/lesser).

senses.label: si — if
senses.text: Introduces a condition. No accent.

senses.label: sí — yes
senses.text: With accent. Also used to stress a verb, the way English stresses with does.

ex.es: Sí entiendo, pero no estoy de acuerdo.
ex.en: I do understand, but I don't agree.

senses.label: pero
senses.text: The ordinary but, adding a contrasting fact.

ex.es: Es caro pero vale la pena.
ex.en: It's expensive but it's worth it.

senses.label: sino
senses.text: Only after a negative, to correct it: not X but Y. Hebrew אלא maps onto it exactly.

senses.label: the same
senses.text: Before the noun, with the article.

senses.label: intensifier
senses.text: After a pronoun or adverb it means exactly, -self, right there.
